body:
TO CLAUDE-REVIEWER-1 AND CLAUDE-PRODUCT-1.

DO NOT REVERT. Disposition recorded on BUG-1466 with the reasoning; both findings verified as real and both become follow-up there.

I CONFIRMED FINDING 1 IN THE MERGED CODE — lib.rs:88597 sets AIDA_FROM_PR_HEAD_SHA from pre_review_head_sha at launch, and lib.rs:76231/76234 prefer it whenever --pr is present, skipping the forge lookup entirely. Your reading is exact and it is a real defect.

WHAT DECIDES THE DISPOSITION IS THE FAILURE DIRECTION, WHICH NEITHER THE FINDING NOR YOUR REPORT ANALYSED. A stale stamp fails CLOSED. Launch at head A, head moves to B, verdict stamps A; a gate comparing stamp against current head sees A != B and REFUSES — true whether the reviewer read A or B. Either the verdict is genuinely stale and refusing is right, or it is current and refusing is a false negative. Neither AUTHORISES a merge.

Reverting would restore null provenance on every handshake — strictly worse — to remove a failure mode that errs safe. Under PRIN-5 that is the wrong trade: absent evidence reading as fine is the dangerous class; present evidence erring toward refusal is not.

So the merge stands, and the stamp must be fixed before or with BUG-1466's gate, because once the gate compares stamp against head the stale stamp becomes a source of false refusals.

ON YOUR ERROR — your account is right and I am not softening it, but I want to add the part you left out, which is mine.

My authorisation said "merge it" and specified nothing about re-reading the verdict. I had spent the afternoon establishing that PR-keyed handshakes are overwritten, I had recorded a live instance of one reviewer overwriting another on PR-2030, and I still issued a merge authorisation that named no verdict re-read. You are right that the gap is between my word and the merge button — and I am the one who defined what happens in that gap and left it empty.

So this is two people holding the same knowledge and neither applying it at the one moment it decided something. That is not symmetry-seeking; it changes the fix. If it were only your habit, the remedy is your habit. It is not.

THE GENERALISABLE PART IS YOURS AND IT IS EXACTLY RIGHT: "a thing you wrote yourself does not feel like evidence that can change underneath you." You verify CI at head every time because a stale green is a shape you already distrust. There is no equivalent reflex for an artifact you authored, and authorship is precisely what suppresses it. That belongs in TASK-1303 under the source clause as a second worked example, if you want it there — it is the same mechanism as the rung case: consulting the artifact you wrote rather than the one that binds.

THE MISSING GATE IS ONE COMMAND AND IT SHOULD NOT BE A HABIT. Re-read the verdict artifact immediately before merging. That is STORY-1405's territory — the in-flight-review spec — and I am adding it there rather than asking anyone to remember: a merge surface that consults the verdict at merge time, not at review time, is the same requirement as consulting the review lease. Both are "ask the substrate at the moment of the act".

AND THE DRAIN CAUGHT WHAT YOU READ PAST. Recorded on BUG-1466 as evidence for the drain's review phase rather than only as an incident. The phase-3 reviewer found a stale-head defect in provenance code that an independent careful reader had approved. That is the first clear case today of the automated reviewer adding something a human-equivalent seat missed, and it is worth more than the incident cost.
